title: An expired reservation stops blocking the path it no longer holds
action: A dead session's reservation outlives its own TTL and blocks the exact path it named. The conflict PRE-CHECK is expiry-aware: list_reservations(.., active_only = true) drops expired leases (leases.rs:330-338), so an expired lease is not a logical conflict. But the O_EXCL create still collides with the stale file on disk, and the AlreadyExists arm (reserve.rs:309-330) reads that lease and reports it as a conflict WITHOUT ever consulting `expires_at`. So a path whose holder died is refused past its TTL, and nothing clears it automatically — unlike cell claims, which are swept at three doors (orient.rs:274, recovery_verb.rs:221, handlers_select.rs:662), reservations have no sweep door at all: lease_store.rs:779 `sweep_expired_leases` is reachable only from integration_queue.rs:376 and the manual `bee reservations sweep`. Fix the arm: when the lease parses AND reads expired at `now`, take it over — remove the stale file and retry the create once — instead of reporting a conflict. Reuse the same expiry predicate the pre-check uses (`lease_record_expired`, leases.rs around :316) so the two paths cannot disagree; do not write a second expiry rule. Bound it: retry the create exactly once, and if that retry also loses the race, report the conflict as before — a live competitor must never be stolen from, and an unparseable lease is never guessed at (the existing `Err(_) => None` at reserve.rs:324 stays as-is, reporting a null holder). Then give reservations the door they lack, mirroring the claim sweep: call `sweep_expired_leases` from `bee orient` where the claim sweep already runs (verbs/status_full/orient.rs:274), so takeover is the rare path rather than the normal one. Keep `reserve_exact_path_race_reports_conflict` (tests.rs:145-165) passing untouched — a LIVE holder must still produce exactly that refusal — and add its counterpart: an expired lease on the same path is taken over and the new reserve succeeds.

truths: An expired lease on the exact path is taken over and the new reservation succeeds
A live lease on the exact path still refuses with the same conflict output as before
The takeover uses the same expiry predicate as the active_only pre-check, not a second rule
The create is retried at most once, and a lost retry reports a conflict
An unparseable lease is still reported rather than deleted
bee orient sweeps expired leases the way it already sweeps expired claims

artifacts.substantive: expiry-aware takeover in the AlreadyExists arm with a single bounded retry
the expired-lease sweep called at the orient door beside the claim sweep
tests for takeover, live-holder refusal, bounded retry, and unparseable lease
